items.readme:
# AI Pose Gallery · 中文版

> 288 组 / 1439 张 AI 人体姿势参考图，日文数据完整汉化，附可直接部署的响应式静态画廊。

![画廊预览](docs/preview.jpg)

<details><summary>手机端预览</summary>

![手机端预览](docs/mobile.jpg)

</details>

**在线演示：** <https://ai-pose-gallery.anhao.app/>
**原始站点：** <https://ai-pose-gallery.pages.dev/>
**原作者：** ギア（@giaaibusi）
**中文版维护：** Anhao · [X @anhao_ai](https://x.com/anhao_ai)
**GitHub：** <https://github.com/anhao/ai-pose-gallery-zh>

---

## 这是什么

原站是一套面向 AI 绘画 / 3D / 摄影参考的姿势图库，元数据全部为日文，且不提供批量素材下载。本仓库做了三件事：

1. **全量镜像** —— 1439 条记录对应的 1439 张缩略图（JPG 300×400）与 1439 张原图（PNG 900×1200）全部落地，共 2878 个文件 / 659.5 MB。
2. **完整汉化** —— 日文字段逐条译为中文，覆盖 4 个体系、26 个分类、288 个姿势名、5 个视角，零遗漏。
3. **可用的前端** —— 零依赖响应式画廊，完整实现原站的分类筛选、多角度切换、分组浏览、灯箱导航与原图下载，并针对手机重新设计布局。

## 页面功能

- 4 个体系页签，显示各体系的图片数与姿势组数
- 姿势名、编号、ID、分类关键词搜索，支持 `/` 快速聚焦
- 动作分类、5 种视角组合筛选，可一键重置
- **按姿势分组 / 逐张浏览**双模式，分组卡片带多角度缩略图
- 悬停或点击缩略图切换主图角度，点击卡片打开灯箱
- 灯箱先显示缩略图、再加载 900×1200 原图，支持直接下载 PNG、复制 ID、新窗口打开
- `← / →` 切换角度，`↑ / ↓` 切换姿势，`Esc` 关闭；手机支持左右滑动
- PC 多列网格、手机双列网格，移动端筛选面板可展开/收起
- 使用指南与注意事项弹窗，页脚标注图片来源与维护者链接

## SEO 与分享

页面内置了完整的 SEO 与社交分享配置：

- 关键词化标题：`AI 姿势参考库｜288 组人体姿势 · 1439 张多角度参考图`
- 独立 description、keywords、author 与 `max-image-preview:large`
- `canonical` 指向正式域名，避免自定义域名与 pages.dev 域名重复收录
- Open Graph / Twitter Card 使用 1200×630 的 `og-cover.jpg`
- JSON-LD 结构化数据：`WebSite` + `ImageGallery`，声明语言、简介与页面主图
- `robots.txt` 放行全站并声明 sitemap，`sitemap.xml` 指向首页
- 语义结构：单一 H1、分区 H2、卡片 H3；缩略图 `alt` 含姿势名与视角，图片懒加载

仓库中的绝对地址统一指向 `https://ai-pose-gallery.anhao.app/`。Fork 后如使用其他域名，需同步替换 `index.html` 的 canonical、`og:*`、`twitter:*`、JSON-LD，以及 `robots.txt`、`sitemap.xml` 中的地址。

## 数据规模

| 体系 | 条数 |
| --- | ---: |
| 全身单人・标准系 | 365 |
| 全身单人・性感系 | 399 |
| 上半身单人 | 400 |
| 双人缠绵 | 275 |
| **合计** | **1439** |

每条记录对应 5 个视角中的若干个：正面 / 斜侧 / 侧面 / 俯视 / 仰视。

## 目录结构

```
.
├── index.html              # 单页画廊（零依赖，直接打开即可）
├── robots.txt              # 搜索引擎抓取规则
├── sitemap.xml             # 站点地图
├── og-cover.jpg            # 1200×630 社交分享封面
├── data/
│   ├── pose.json           # 原始日文数据（1439 条，未改动）
│   ├── pose-zh.json        # 中文数据（前端实际读取，含检索字段）
│   ├── meta.json           # 原始体系分类
│   ├── meta-zh.json        # 中文体系分类
│   └── translations.csv    # 日⇄中对照表（323 条，便于校对）
├── thumbs/                 # 缩略图 1439 张 JPG 300×400（22 MB）
├── img/                    # 原图 1439 张 PNG 900×1200（637 MB）
├── scripts/
│   ├── download.py         # 并发下载器（48 线程 / 断点续传 / 自动重试）
│   ├── i18n.py             # 日译中词典（唯一值去重后的 323 条译文）
│   ├── apply_translation.py# 回填译文，生成中文数据
│   ├── verify.py           # 校验文件完整性（存在性 / 大小 / 图片头）
│   └── build.sh            # 生成 Cloudflare Pages 发布目录 dist/
├── docs/                   # README 页面预览图
├── _headers                # Cloudflare Pages 缓存策略
├── LICENSE
└── README.md
```

## 数据结构

`data/pose-zh.json` 字段说明：

| 字段 | 原日文字段 | 示例 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | — | `full_sexy_P001_front` | 唯一标识 |
| `体系` | `系統` | 全身单人・性感系 | 4 大类 |
| `姿势编号` | `ポーズ番号` | `P001` | 80 组编号 |
| `分类` | `分類` | 站姿 | 26 类动作 |
| `姿势名称` | `ポーズ名` | S形站姿・胯部侧顶 | 288 种描述 |
| `角度` | `アングル` | 正面 | 5 种视角 |
| `缩略图` | `サムネ` | `thumbs/…jpg` | 相对路径 |
| `原图` | `原寸` | `img/…png` | 相对路径 |
| `检索` | — | 拼接串 | 供前端模糊搜索 |

原始日文数据 `data/pose.json` 保持原样，字段名与站点接口一致，便于对照或回灌。

## 本地预览

画廊通过 `fetch` 读取 JSON，需要 HTTP 环境（直接双击 `index.html` 会被 CORS 拦截）：

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 打开 http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

页面支持体系/分类/视角组合筛选、关键词搜索、分组与逐张浏览、多角度缩略图、懒加载、灯箱原图下载、键盘与触屏导航。

## 脚本用法

```bash
# 重新拉取全部图片（已存在的文件自动跳过，可反复执行）
python3 scripts/download.py
WORKERS=64 python3 scripts/download.py   # 调整并发

# 修改 scripts/i18n.py 中的译文后，重新生成中文数据
python3 scripts/apply_translation.py

# 校验 2878 个文件是否完整
python3 scripts/verify.py
```

## 部署到 Cloudflare Pages

仓库为纯静态站点，无框架、无依赖。

**方式一：GitHub 自动部署（推荐）**

1. 登录 Cloudflare Dashboard → **Workers & Pages** → **Create** → **Pages** → **Connect to Git**
2. 选择本仓库 → 生产分支 `main`
3. 构建设置照抄：

   | 字段 | 值 |
   | --- | --- |
   | Framework preset | `None` |
   | Build command | `bash scripts/build.sh` |
   | Build output directory | `dist` |

4. **Save and Deploy**，约 2–5 分钟得到 `https://<project>.pages.dev`
5. 之后每次 `git push` 自动重新发布

> ⚠️ **不要**把 Build output directory 直接填 `/`。仓库根目录含 `.git`（数百 MB），
> Cloudflare 会把它当静态资源扫描，pack 文件超过 25 MiB 单文件限制会导致构建失败。
> `scripts/build.sh` 只拷贝 `index.html`、`_headers`、`data/`、`thumbs/`、`img/` 到 `dist/`。
> 若确实想用根目录，仓库已附 `.assetsignore` 兜底排除非站点文件。

> 站点限制：单文件 ≤ 25 MiB、每次部署 ≤ 20,000 个文件。本仓库最大文件 917 KB、共 2883 个文件，均在限制内。

**方式二：命令行直传**

```bash
bash scripts/build.sh
npx wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name ai-pose-gallery-zh
```

`_headers` 已为 `img/`、`thumbs/` 配置一年期强缓存，图片不会重复回源。

## 内容提示

图库包含成人向姿势参考（部分分类名称涉及性行为术语），仅供艺术创作、动作参考与前端技术学习使用。请勿用于违法用途。未成年人请勿访问。

## 版权与致谢

- **图片与原始数据的著作权归原作者ギア所有**，来源地址见页首
- 本仓库仅为个人学习、汉化与静态站点实践存档，**不对图片主张任何权利**，也不构成对原作品的商业使用授权
- 若原作者认为本仓库侵犯其权益，请通过 Issue 联系，将立即删除相关内容
- `scripts/` 与 `index.html` 的代码以 MIT 协议开源（见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)），该协议**不覆盖** `img/`、`thumbs/` 与 `data/` 中的图片和原始数据

items.description: Create Apple style dimensional drawings of UI components.
items.readme:
dimensional-drawing ✏️📐

Give it a UI component, get back a one-page technical drawing of it.
Paddings, gaps, corner radii, layers and viewport placement, measured and labeled like Apple's dimensional drawings.

Install · Use it · Make it move · Examples

--- Apple publishes [dimensional drawings](https://developer.apple.com/accessories/dimensional-drawings/) for every device so accessory makers can build cases that fit. They are calm, dense and beautiful: one sheet, a few views, tiny detail circles, numbers everywhere. This repo teaches your agent to draw **your components** the same way. A card or a dialog becomes a spec sheet you could hand to anyone and they would rebuild its *architecture*: paddings, gaps, radii, layers, how it sits in the viewport. Copy and content are left out on purpose, so the drawing stays true when the text changes. ## What's inside 🎁 ``` skills/ ├── dimensional-drawing/ the drawing skill │ ├── SKILL.md │ └── examples/ card + dialog sheets (single HTML files) └── dimensional-drawing-motion/ turns a sheet into a ~10 s film ├── SKILL.md ├── templates/ reference scene + stylesheet └── adapters/ ├── claude-motion.md Claude's Motion artifact (primary) └── headless/ Playwright + ffmpeg, no Claude needed ``` ### The house rules | | | |---|---| | ⚫️ **Monochrome** | grays only; things are told apart by line weight, dashes and hatches | | 🧱 **Architecture, not content** | `TITLE SLOT · FLEX`, `ACTION · HUG`, `CONTENT SLOT · FILL` | | 🔤 **Variables, not numbers** | `S1`, `R2`, `H1 = 2·S1 + H3`, `R2 = R1 − B − S6` | | 🏷️ **Unbranded** | neutral names like `UI-CARD-001` | | 🙅 **Never invent values** | unknowns stay `[TBD]` | ## Install **Claude Code** ```bash git clone https://github.com/enesozturk/dimensional-drawing cp -r dimensional-drawing/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/ ``` **claude.ai / Claude desktop:** zip a skill folder (for example `skills/dimensional-drawing`) and add it under *Settings → Capabilities → Skills*. **Any other agent** (Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, …): use the [`skills`](https://skills.sh) CLI, or point your agent at the `SKILL.md` files. ```bash npx skills add enesozturk/dimensional-drawing ``` ## Use it Ask for a drawing and point at the source (a repo file, a Storybook story, a URL, a screenshot): > Make a dimensional drawing of the `Card` component in `src/components/Card.tsx` > Draw the anatomy of our settings dialog, same style as the examples You get a title block with the key variables on top, then one dense sheet: notes, plan view, exploded layers, detail views (nested corner, radii, body), and variable tables. It works for physical things too (third-angle views, mm, published specs only). Try a thermos 🫖. ## Make it move 🎬 The motion skill animates a finished sheet like a pen drawing it while a camera moves over the paper: 1. close-up on the header as its lines draw in 2. pull back to the plan view while the rest draws 3. layers lift off the plan into the exploded view (strokes first, fills after, so nothing flashes) 4. pull back to the full sheet as the remaining views draw in The scene is a pure function of time, so it runs in two places: | | | |---|---| | **With Claude** | ask *"animate this drawing"*. Claude builds it in the **Motion** artifact and you export MP4. This is the primary target and where the timing was tuned. | | **Without Claude** | `cd skills/dimensional-drawing-motion/adapters/headless && npm install`, then `node render.mjs --scene ../../templates/scene-dialog.js --css ../../templates/base.css --out dialog.mp4`. Needs Node 18+ and ffmpeg. | > [!NOTE] > Optimized for Claude Motion. The headless renderer is tested with Playwright (Chromium) + ffmpeg. Other animation libraries (Remotion, Motion Canvas, GSAP, Lottie…) are **not tested**. ## Examples **Dialog**: fixed width, scrim, viewport placement, header controls, footer actions **Card**: flexible width, body well, nested corner, shadow envelope Open the HTML versions in [`skills/dimensional-drawing/examples`](skills/dimensional-drawing/examples). items.readme: # Beautiful Rust Three standard [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) and a lints config that teach coding agents to write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Rust: - **`rust-best-practices`** loads whenever an agent writes or changes Rust, and steers it toward idiomatic, robust, maintainable code. - **`rust-review`** reviews existing Rust code, a file, a crate, or a diff, and writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix. - **`rust-port`** ports C, C++, Python, Go, or JavaScript to idiomatic Rust with the same behavior, porting the original tests first so you can prove the two match. - **`lints/`** is a drop-in clippy configuration that enforces the machine-checkable rules in CI. They work with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and any other agent that reads the Agent Skills format. Every code example in the skills compiles on stable Rust, and every lint in the config was checked against current clippy. The guidance is distilled from five sources, with a condensed digest of each bundled in the skill so the agent can consult the original reasoning when it needs to: - [Google Rust Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/rustguide.html) - [Rust API Guidelines](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/) (official rust-lang checklist) - [Effective Rust](https://www.lurklurk.org/effective-rust/) by David Drysdale - [Rust Design Patterns](https://rust-unofficial.github.io/patterns/) (idioms, patterns, anti-patterns) - [Microsoft Pragmatic Rust Guidelines](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/) Where the sources disagree, the skill picks a side and says why. ## What it changes Asked for a small semver-parsing library, an agent without the skill produced working code with public fields, no `# Errors` docs, and `unwrap()` in its doc examples. With the skill, the same agent kept the fields private, documented failure modes, and wrote doc examples users can copy safely. Condensed from those two runs: ```rust // Without the skill /// A semantic version. The fields are public for convenience. pub struct Version { pub major: u64, pub minor: u64, pub patch: u64, pub pre: Vec, pub build: Vec, } impl Version { /// Parses a version string. /// /// ``` /// let v = Version::parse("1.2.3").unwrap(); /// ``` pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result { /* ... */ } } ``` ```rust // With the skill /// A semantic version. Equality, hashing, and ordering ignore build metadata. pub struct Version { major: u64, minor: u64, patch: u64, pre: Vec, build: Vec, } impl Version { /// Parses a version string according to SemVer 2.0.0. /// /// # Errors /// /// Returns [`ParseVersionError`] if the string is empty, a numeric part has a /// leading zero or overflows `u64`, or an identifier contains invalid characters. /// /// ``` /// # use semver_lite::Version; /// # fn main() -> Result<(), semver_lite::ParseVersionError> { /// let v = Version::parse("1.2.3-beta.1")?; /// assert_eq!(v.major(), 1); /// # Ok(()) /// # } /// ``` pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result { /* ... */ } /// Returns the major version number. pub fn major(&self) -> u64 { self.major } } ``` Across three test tasks (a library, a CLI, and refactoring a messy module), the skill passed 29 of 30 checks against 24 of 30 without it. See [Testing the skills](#testing-the-skills). ## Install Each skill is a folder under `skills/`: `rust-best-practices/`, `rust-review/`, and `rust-port/`. Every option below puts those folders where your agent looks for skills. Install all three; the review and port skills lean on the best-practices skill for style. ### Any agent, one command The [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installer supports most agents (Node 22.20 or later): ```bash npx skills add morganlinton/BeautifulRust ``` Add `-g` to install for your user instead of the current project, or `-a ` to pick an agent, such as `-a codex` or `-a cursor`. ### Claude Code Install it as a plugin so updates arrive with one command: ```bash claude plugin install beautiful-rust --marketplace morganlinton/BeautifulRust ``` Inside a session, the same thing is: ``` /plugin marketplace add morganlinton/BeautifulRust /plugin install beautiful-rust@beautiful-rust ``` This installs all three skills. They appear as `/beautiful-rust:rust-best-practices`, `/beautiful-rust:rust-review`, and `/beautiful-rust:rust-port`, though you rarely need to call them, since they trigger on their own. To try it for one session without installing, clone the repo and run `claude --plugin-dir ./BeautifulRust`. ### GitHub Copilot With GitHub CLI 2.90 or later: ```bash gh skill install morganlinton/BeautifulRust rust-best-practices gh skill install morganlinton/BeautifulRust rust-review gh skill install morganlinton/BeautifulRust rust-port ``` This installs into the current project by default. Add `--scope user` to install for your user, or `--agent ` to install for a different agent. ### Gemini CLI ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/morganlinton/BeautifulRust --path skills/rust-best-practices gemini skills install https://github.com/morganlinton/BeautifulRust --path skills/rust-review gemini skills install https://github.com/morganlinton/BeautifulRust --path skills/rust-port ``` ### OpenAI Codex, Cursor, or anything else: copy the folder Clone the repo and copy the three skill folders into your agent's skills directory. Most agents now read the shared `.agents/skills/` location: ```bash git clone https://github.com/morganlinton/BeautifulRust mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills cp -R BeautifulRust/skills/rust-* ~/.agents/skills/ ``` | Agent | User directory | Project directory | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` | `.claude/skills/` | | OpenAI Codex | `~/.agents/skills/` | `.agents/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `~/.copilot/skills/` or `~/.agents/skills/` | `.github/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` | | Cursor | `~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.agents/skills/` | `.cursor/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` | | Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/skills/` or `~/.agents/skills/` | `.gemini/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` | Claude Code does not read `.agents/skills/`, so use its own directory or the plugin. Restart the agent if the skill doesn't show up right away. ### claude.ai claude.ai takes one zip per skill, with the skill folder as the zip root: ```bash cd skills zip -r ../rust-best-practices.zip rust-best-practices -x '*.DS_Store' -x '*/evals/*' zip -r ../rust-review.zip rust-review -x '*.DS_Store' -x '*/evals/*' zip -r ../rust-port.zip rust-port -x '*.DS_Store' -x '*/evals/*' ``` Upload each under **Customize > Skills**. Code execution must be enabled first. ## Reviewing existing code Ask your agent to review a file, crate, or diff, for example "review src/parser.rs" or "what would you change in this PR". The `rust-review` skill runs `cargo fmt`, `clippy`, and the tests when a toolchain is available, then writes a report with three tiers: must fix, should fix, and consider. Every finding gives a `file:line` location, the rule it breaks with its source (an API Guidelines code such as `C-GETTER`, an Effective Rust item, a Microsoft guideline, or a clippy lint), and the smallest code change that fixes it. Each report ends with what the code already does well. [`examples/review-inventory.md`](examples/review-inventory.md) is a real review the skill produced for the deliberately messy module in the eval cases. ## Porting code to Rust Ask your agent to port a module, for example "port parser.c to Rust" or "rewrite this Python service in Rust". The `rust-port` skill reads the original and its tests, ports the tests first, designs a Rust API instead of transliterating the original, and verifies with `cargo test` and `clippy`. It maps each language's habits to their Rust equivalents: `NULL` and `None` to `Option`, error codes and exceptions to an error enum, out-parameters to return values, flag ints and magic strings to typed enums and options, and dict insertion order to an ordered collection instead of a `HashMap` that would silently reorder output. Each port comes with a `PORTING.md` that maps the old API and tests to the new ones and lists every deliberate difference. ## Bevy Bevy calls your systems and builds their arguments, so some general Rust advice is wrong for them. Taken at face value, the skills would tell an agent to change `Res` to a reference, replace `use bevy::prelude::*` with explicit imports, and split a system to quiet clippy. When a crate depends on `bevy` or `bevy_ecs`, both the writing and review skills now read [`references/bevy.md`](skills/rust-best-practices/references/bevy.md) first. It covers Bevy 0.20 and does two things: - **It names the conventions to leave alone:** system parameters taken by value, the Bevy prelude, public fields on plain-data components, and complex query types. - **It lists the ECS bugs that compile cleanly.** Two queries that can both mutate the same component panic with error B0001 on the first frame. A system can read the world before another system's `Commands` have applied. Systems that depend on each other may have no order between them. A `.single().unwrap()` crashes the game once the player dies. Every behavior in the reference was checked with a test against bevy 0.20.0. Two eval cases cover it: a review of a combat plugin with two of those bugs planted, and a feature added to the fixed plugin, which checks that the agent keeps Bevy's conventions. ## Enforcing the rules with clippy The skills teach the rules; the lints keep them from slipping back in. Copy [`lints/clippy.toml`](lints/clippy.toml) next to your `Cargo.toml` and paste the `[lints]` block from [`lints/lints.toml`](lints/lints.toml) into it, then run: ```bash cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings ``` It flags `unwrap()` outside tests, `unsafe` blocks without a `// SAFETY:` comment, `#[allow]` without a reason, any `bool` function parameter, silent lossy `as` casts, missing `# Errors` and `# Panics` docs, and leftover `dbg!` and `todo!`. Lints marked `[lib]` in the file are for libraries, and applications can drop them. Bevy crates need four extra allows, listed in the [Bevy reference](skills/rust-best-practices/references/bevy.md#keep-bevys-conventions), because the table otherwise flags every idiomatic system signature. Every lint in the table is proven to fire. [`lints/check/`](lints/check/src/lib.rs) is a small crate with one deliberate violation per lint, and this script runs clippy on it from the repo root: ```bash bash scripts/check-lints.sh ``` It fails if a lint stops firing, if something unexpected fires, or if the check crate's copy of the table drifts from `lints/lints.toml`. `allow_attributes` and `allow_attributes_without_reason` need `rust-version = "1.81"` or later, because clippy switches them off for crates that can't use `#[expect]`. ## What the writing skill covers `skills/rust-best-practices/SKILL.md` is about 500 lines, organized so an agent can scan it while coding: 1. Mindset: Rust-shaped code, invalid states unrepresentable, application vs library 2. Pre-handback checklist: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, test, doc; lint policy 3. Ownership and borrowing: what to do instead of cloning for the borrow checker 4. Types and API design: naming, newtypes, common traits, builders, visibility, generics vs `dyn` 5. Errors and panics: `Option` vs `Result` vs panic, library vs application error types 6. Everyday idioms: iterators, combinators, `format!`, imports, drop guards 7. Concurrency and async: `Send` assertions, lock discipline, `async fn`, yield points 8. Unsafe and FFI: when it's allowed, `SAFETY:` comments, soundness, bindgen 9. Crates, modules, dependencies: workspace layout, features, semver 10. Documentation and comments 11. Tests 12. Performance, in order 13. Final checklist `skills/rust-best-practices/references/` holds one digest per source for deeper lookups. ## Layout ``` BeautifulRust/ ├── .claude-plugin/ │ ├── plugin.json plugin manifest │ └── marketplace.json lets this repo act as its own marketplace ├── skills/ │ ├── rust-best-practices/ writing skill │ │ ├── SKILL.md │ │ ├── references/ one digest per source, plus bevy.md │ │ └── evals/ │ ├── rust-review/ review skill │ │ ├── SKILL.md │ │ └── evals/ │ └── rust-port/ porting skill │ ├── SKILL.md │ └── evals/ a C module and a Python module to port ├── lints/ │ ├── lints.toml [lints] block for Cargo.toml │ ├── clippy.toml clippy thresholds │ └── check/ one deliberate violation per lint ├── scripts/ │ ├── check-skill.py validates skills, evals, and manifests │ ├── check-lints.sh proves every lint in the table fires │ ├── check-examples.py compiles every Rust example in the docs │ └── examples.json context that lets fragment examples compile ├── benchmarks/ │ └── cross-agent-2026-10/ Claude Code vs Codex, with and without the skills ├── examples/ │ └── review-inventory.md a real review report ├── CHANGELOG.md ├── CONTRIBUTING.md └── README.md ``` ## Testing the skills `skills/rust-best-practices/evals/` holds four test cases in the layout `claude plugin eval` reads: a library API design task, an application CLI task, and a refactor-this-module task with an input file. Each case has the prompt, a description of a good result, and one assertion per file under `graders/`. Run them with and without the skill from the skill directory: ```bash claude plugin eval . --allow-tools Write,Edit,Bash --scaffold ``` `skills/rust-review/evals/` holds a review case for the same messy module and one for a Bevy plugin with two ECS bugs planted, and `skills/rust-port/evals/` holds a C module and a Python module to port, each with its original test suite. The writing skill also has a Bevy case that adds a feature to a working plugin. Run them the same way from each skill's directory. These are real model runs and are billed. **Across agents.** The [October 2026 benchmark](benchmarks/cross-agent-2026-10/README.md) ran all eight cases on Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex CLI, with and without the skills, and graded the results blind: | | No skills | Skills | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code (Opus 5.5) | 72/85 (85%) | 80/85 (94%) | | Codex CLI (default model) | 53/85 (62%) | 76/85 (89%) | The skills helped Codex more than Claude, and helped reviews most. They hurt in one case: Claude did worse on the Bevy feature task with them. The benchmark page has the details, the method, and the caveats. Notably, it was one run per configuration, graded by a Claude model. ## Updating Edit the skill, bump `version` in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, commit, and push. Claude Code plugin users pick up the new version with: ```bash claude plugin update beautiful-rust ``` Anyone who copied the folder or used an installer re-runs the install command. Record each release in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Validate before pushing. `python3 scripts/check-skill.py` checks skill frontmatter, links, eval cases, and plugin manifests. Pass `--json` for machine-readable output. `python3 scripts/check-examples.py` compiles every Rust block in the skills, reference digests, README, and examples with `cargo check`. ```bash python3 scripts/check-skill.py python3 scripts/check-examples.py claude plugin validate . ``` ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Every rule needs a published source; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to propose a rule, report a review false positive, or add an eval case. ## Sources and attribution The guidance in this skill is a synthesis. The five digests in `skills/rust-best-practices/references/` are paraphrased summaries written for this project; they restate each source's advice in condensed form and link back to the original. Read the originals for the full reasoning. | Source | Author | License | |---|---|---| | [Google Rust Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/rustguide.html) | Google | CC BY 3.0 | | [Rust API Guidelines](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/) | The Rust Project | MIT or Apache-2.0 | | [Effective Rust](https://www.lurklurk.org/effective-rust/) | David Drysdale, published by O'Reilly | CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (online edition) | | [Rust Design Patterns](https://rust-unofficial.github.io/patterns/) | rust-unofficial contributors | MPL-2.0 | | [Pragmatic Rust Guidelines](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/) | Microsoft | MIT | The skill text, the digests, the banner, and the generator script in this repository are MIT licensed (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). The crab is a crab, not the Rust mascot. ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# Digital Human Koubo · AI 数字人口播 **One photo + one sentence → a finished talking-head video with a digital human.** Script, lip-synced AI presenter, voice clean-up, captions, and pro-YouTuber-style packaging — fully automated by your AI agent. **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-black.svg)](LICENSE) ![Agent Skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent%20Skill-SKILL.md-orange) [![Renoise MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/video-Renoise%20MCP-ff7a1a)](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) ![Remotion](https://img.shields.io/badge/edit-Remotion%204-0b84f3)
> This 27-second livestream ad has no real presenter. Face, voice, studio, captions and the price animation are all AI. > The only input was one sentence: *"Use this digital human to make a 30-second livestream ad for the WorkBuddy course — 10 lessons, ¥99, was ¥999."* > Total cost: **482 [Renoise](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) credits**. --- ## Demos Click a GIF (or "Watch") to play the full video. Every demo below was produced with this repo. | | | | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | | **Livestream sales ad** · 9:16 · 27 s
Style B + depth-text price ¥999→¥99
[▶ Watch](https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo/releases/download/v1.0.0/workbuddy-live-ad.mp4) | **Product recommendation** · 9:16 · 89 s

Vision person matting, 3-layer composite
[▶ Watch](https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo/releases/download/v1.0.0/text-behind.mp4) | | | | |:---:|:---:| | | | | **Step-by-step tutorial** · 16:9 · 4:36
The digital human teaches how she was made (Style D)

Two presenters, 6 languages, 4 scenes, cat & dog (Style E)
[▶ Watch](https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo/releases/download/v1.0.0/tutorial-digital-human-upgrade.mp4) | | | | | **Launch breakdown** · 16:9 · 39 s
Presenter on the side, code B-roll on the right (Style C)

Packaging component gallery · 48 components · 2:40 · ▶ Watch
> All presenters in the demos are AI digital humans and every video is labelled "内容由 AI 数字人演绎" (performed by an AI digital human). The male presenter is the author's own digital twin, made from his own photo. --- ## What it does - **Digital human from one photo** — a fixed presenter (face, outfit, voice description, prompt template) stored in `persona.json`, so every video is the same person. Composite her into any scene (livestream studio, shop, classroom, Kyoto street) with GPT Image first, then make her talk. - **Lip-synced talking clips** — the script is split into ≤ 15-second segments and generated with **Grok Video 1.5** through **[Renoise MCP](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official)**. Other models (Wan 3.0, OmniHuman for your own recording) are documented. - **Cost gate** — the agent always quotes *segments · seconds · credits · balance* first and waits for your "yes". It generates segment 1 for you to check before batching the rest. - **Quality control** — every segment is transcribed with whisper and compared with the script, and 4 frames per segment are inspected (Grok sometimes burns subtitles into the picture; those segments get re-shot). - **Voice unification** — 1/3-octave spectral matching, de-essing, one shared small-room reverb and loudness normalisation, so 30 separately-generated clips sound like one recording (sibilance spread 13.2 dB → 5.9 dB in our tests). - **5 editing styles, chosen for your content** — the agent diagnoses your content, recommends 2 styles with preview images and asks you everything in one go (style · ratio & length · caption intensity · presenter). - **48 packaging components** — measured frame-by-frame from 25 videos by top creators (MrBeast, Mark Rober, Ryan Trahan, MKBHD, MediaStorm/影视飓风, 何同学, Johnny Harris, Vox, Kurzgesagt, 回形针, 半佛仙人, 差评, 毕导). Each style has a default packaging recipe; add or remove techniques by just asking. - **Text behind the presenter** — big words / numbers between the background and the person (macOS Vision person segmentation → transparent video → 3-layer composite). - **Multi-language** — English, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, Arabic tested (whisper back-check 94–100 %). - **Works with your agent** — a standard `SKILL.md` Agent Skill plus scripts; any agent that can load skills, connect a remote MCP server and run local commands can drive it. ## How it works ``` your content ──► 0. setup check (Renoise MCP / ffmpeg / whisper — skip what you already have) 1. diagnose content → recommend 2 of 5 styles → ask once → brief.json 2. script.json (≤15 s per segment, ~5.4 Chinese chars/s) 3. quote credits → wait for "yes" → generate segment 1 → you check → batch 4. range-download (CDN-safe) → whisper back-check → frame check 5. voice unification (spectral match + de-ess + shared room) 6. word-level timeline (tl.json) 7. edit in Remotion: style template + default packaging (+ your requests) 8. render → check mid-transition frames → loudness (-14 / -16 LUFS) ```

--- ## Supported agents The skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` (the open Agent Skills format) plus Python / shell / Remotion scripts. To run the **whole** pipeline an agent needs three things: 1. **Load Agent Skills** (a skills folder or skill upload), 2. **Connect a remote MCP server** (Renoise — streamable HTTP, browser login, no API key), 3. **Run commands on your computer** (ffmpeg, Python, Node — for downloading, QA and editing). | Agent | Skills | Renoise MCP | Local commands | Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | `~/.claude/skills/` | `/plugin` (below) | ✅ | ✅ Tested — this repo was built with it | | **Codex** (CLI / desktop) | `~/.codex/skills/` | `codex mcp add` | ✅ | ✅ Expected to work (same scripts) | | **OpenClaw** | skills folder per OpenClaw docs | `openclaw plugins install` | ✅ | ⚙️ Should work | | **WorkBuddy** | Skills → import the folder / zip | Connectors → add custom MCP | ✅ desktop agent | ⚙️ Should work — menu names may differ by version | | **豆包 (Doubao)** · **千问办公 (Qwen Office)** · **纳米Work (NamiWork)** and other agent products | import if the product supports Agent Skills | add as a custom / remote MCP server if supported | needed for editing | ⚙️ Works if the product supports the 3 requirements above; check its docs | | **Claude desktop / claude.ai** | upload the skill zip in Settings | Connectors → Add custom connector | ⚠️ sandbox only | Script writing, scene design, generation & quoting work; local editing needs a shell agent | > If your agent can only do MCP + chat (no local commands), you can still use it to **plan, quote and generate** the clips through Renoise; then run the editing steps with Claude Code / Codex, or by hand with the commands in [`SKILL.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/SKILL.md). --- ## Installation ### 1 · Get the code ```bash git clone https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo.git cd digital-human-koubo ``` ### 2 · Install the two skills into your agent The repo contains two skills: `digital-human-koubo` (main) and `finance-explainer` (the engine for Style A, the finance / tech explainer). **Claude Code** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -R skills/digital-human-koubo skills/finance-explainer ~/.claude/skills/ ``` **Codex** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.codex/skills && cp -R skills/digital-human-koubo skills/finance-explainer ~/.codex/skills/ ``` **WorkBuddy / OpenClaw / other agents** — zip the two folders and import them in the product's *Skills* page, or copy them into its skills directory (see the product's docs): ```bash cd skills && zip -r ../digital-human-skills.zip digital-human-koubo finance-explainer && cd .. ``` ### 3 · Connect Renoise MCP (AI video / image generation) Create an account at **[renoise.ai](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official)** first. Login is in the browser — you never paste an API key. | Agent | How | |---|---| | Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add ArcoCodes/renoise-plugins-official` then `/plugin install renoise@renoise-plugins-official` | | Codex | `codex mcp add renoise --url https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` then `codex mcp login renoise` | | OpenClaw | `openclaw plugins install renoise --marketplace ArcoCodes/renoise-plugins-official` | | Claude desktop / claude.ai | Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector** → name `Renoise`, URL `https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` | | WorkBuddy, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, 豆包, 千问, 纳米Work, … | add a remote MCP server with URL `https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` (typical config: `{"mcpServers":{"renoise":{"url":"https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp"}}}`) | Latest official instructions: **[renoise.ai/plugin](https://renoise.ai/plugin)**. Check it worked by asking your agent: *"查一下我的 Renoise 余额 / check my Renoise balance."* ### 4 · Local tools (for downloading, QA and editing) | Tool | macOS | Windows | Linux | |---|---|---|---| | ffmpeg | `brew install ffmpeg` | `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` | `sudo apt install ffmpeg` | | Python 3 + numpy + Pillow | `brew install python` then `python3 -m pip install numpy pillow` | `winget install Python.Python.3.12` | `sudo apt install python3-pip` | | Node.js 18+ (Remotion) | `brew install node` | `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` | `nvm install --lts` | | whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli`) | `brew install whisper-cpp` | [Releases](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/releases) | build from [source](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) | | whisper model | [`ggml-medium-q5_0.bin`](https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-medium-q5_0.bin) → `~/models/` (or `export WHISPER_MODEL=/path/to/model.bin`) | same | same | One-command check — it skips what you have and lists install options for what's missing: ```bash bash ~/.claude/skills/digital-human-koubo/scripts/doctor.sh ``` The **text-behind-presenter** effect uses Apple Vision and needs **macOS**; everything else is cross-platform. ### 5 · Sound effects & placeholder music The repo ships **no third-party audio**. Generate an original set of 30 sound effects and a placeholder background track (pure code, no copyright): ```bash python3 ~/.claude/skills/digital-human-koubo/scripts/make_assets.py ``` `new_edit.sh` also runs this automatically for every new project. For a better soundtrack, drop any track you have the rights to at `/public/music/bgm.mp3`. ### 6 · (Optional) Xiaomi MiMo TTS — designed or cloned voices The default voice is Grok's native voice (best lip-sync). For a designed voice, your own cloned voice, or narration-only videos, the skill uses **Xiaomi MiMo TTS**: 1. Register at **[platform.xiaomimimo.com](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/)** and create an API key. At the time of writing Xiaomi offered the TTS models free for a limited time — check the site for current pricing. 2. Put the key in an environment variable, or in `~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env`: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/ai-teardown && cat > ~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env <<'EOF' MIMO_API_KEY=your-key-here MIMO_BASE_URL=https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1 EOF chmod 600 ~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env ``` 3. Only clone **your own** voice or a voice you have explicit permission to use. > Note: Grok generates lip movement from its own voice. Swapping in a different voice afterwards leaves ~100 ms lip offset (fine in picture-in-picture, visible in full-screen close-ups). For your own recording with exact lip-sync, use an audio-driven model such as OmniHuman (documented in the skill). --- ## Quick start Talk to your agent in plain language: ```text 用我的数字人 Skill 讲这段：……（paste your content） Use my digital human skill to make a 30-second livestream ad: WorkBuddy course, 10 lessons, ¥99 (was ¥999). Make a 3-minute explainer about why Silicon Valley Bank collapsed, Xiaolin-style. Add a map route when she mentions these countries. / Put "¥99" behind her. / Add a teaser cold open. 把包装组件图鉴发我看看 (show me the packaging gallery) ``` What happens next: 1. Setup check — anything already installed is skipped. 2. A one-line diagnosis + 2 recommended styles with preview images, and one round of questions. 3. Script + scene design + **credit quote** → you approve → segment 1 → you approve → the rest. 4. QA, voice clean-up, editing with the style's default packaging → the finished MP4. --- ## Make your own digital human 1. Pick a photo: frontal face, even light, hair off the face, mouth closed. **Only your own photo or one you have permission to use.** 2. Ask the agent to generate a 4-view sheet (front, both sides, back) — GPT Image 2.5, 2k, ~23 credits — so the face stays the same from every angle. 3. Compare models with the same image and line (Grok Video 1.5 vs Wan 3.0, 8 s each) and pick one. 4. Upload the reference to Renoise and put its `material:` into `skills/digital-human-koubo/persona.json` (`renoise.reference_material`, or `other_hosts.me` for a second presenter). Details: [`references/new-avatar.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/new-avatar.md). The `material:` IDs in this repo belong to the author's account and won't work on yours — that's expected.

--- ## Five editing styles

| Style | Ratio | Length | Best for | Template | |---|---|---|---|---| | **A** Finance / tech explainer (Xiaolin-style structure) | 16:9 | 3–20 min | events, data, "why…" | `finance-explainer` engine | | **B** Influencer talking head with animated captions | 9:16 | 30–120 s | product picks, sales, opinions | `templates/huazi-916` (data-driven) | | **C** Launch breakdown | 16:9 | 30–90 s | new products / models | `templates/reference/launch-169` | | **D** Step-by-step tutorial | 16:9 | 3–8 min | "how to…", tool setup | `templates/reference/tutorial-169` | | **E** Multi-host · multi-language · multi-scene | 16:9 | 3–7 min | capability demos, going global | `templates/reference/multihost-169` | Style B has three caption intensities — **restrained / standard / lively**:

Style A learns only the *structure and editing grammar* of popular explainer channels. It never uses a real creator's face, voice, set or lines. --- ## 48 packaging components We measured 25 videos frame by frame (shot detection, opening beats, on-screen text, sound) — full reports in [`references/research/`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/research/).

**Rules distilled from the research** ([`packaging-playbook.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/packaging-playbook.md)): - Cut count can be low, but stimulation can't stop: in the first 30 s, something new every 3–5 s. - First 3 s: the claim or the action — no greeting, no logo. - A BGM bed under everything; sound effects only on events (1–3 per minute in Chinese talking-head channels); 0.6–1.0 s of silence right before a reveal. - For a single-camera digital human, the cheapest pacing is **punch-in cuts** on sentence boundaries (1.0× / 1.18× / 1.32×).

| Group | Components | |---|---| | Opening / hooks | TeaserColdOpen · ColdOpenFreeze · SearchTyping · NumberSpike · SlamText · WordStack · TornStrip · **TextBehind** | | Evidence / data | EvidenceCard · DocFocus · SourceDoc · ZoomFocus · Counter · Odometer · GlassPanel · SpecCard · LineDraw · BarCompare · ReviewCards · ArchiveCards · MapRoute · CompareWipe · PaperCollage | | Annotation / people | HandDraw · CalloutPill · LeaderLabel · TypedNameTag · LowerThird · NamePlate · SourceTag · FreezeFrame | | Rhythm / interaction | PunchInHost · KeywordStack · RetentionCaption · TiltLine · Aside · Danmaku · ReactionPop · MemeWindow · PollPop · GlitchInterstitial · HostFloaters · ProgressChapters · ProgressTracker · ChapterCard · RecapBoard · Countdown · GhostWord | Every component is called by name in a `pack` list, with timings written as `"segment:word"` (e.g. `"3:积分"`), and adapts to 9:16 automatically: ```json "pack": [ { "use": "NumberSpike", "at": "1:不到十块钱", "until": "1:end", "text": "¥9.9/节", "label": "一节课" }, { "use": "Danmaku", "items": [{ "t": "真的假的？", "at": "1:" }, { "t": "AI 还能帮我干活？", "at": "1:教你", "hot": true }] }, { "use": "TextBehind", "src": "main.mp4", "cutout": "main_cut_s4.webm", "cutoutFrom": 17.2, "at": "4:", "until": "4:end", "mode": "count", "lines": [{ "t": "¥99", "font": "en", "color": "#FFE14D", "size": 0.17 }], "count": { "from": 999, "to": 99, "prefix": "¥" } } ] ``` Reference: [`references/packaging.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/packaging.md). Validate before rendering: `python3 scripts/check_edit.py /src`. ### Text behind the presenter

```bash python3 scripts/cutout_video.py public/main.mp4 public/main_cut_s4.webm --from 17.2 --to 22.4 # matte only the seconds you need ``` It works on **medium shots with headroom**. In a selfie close-up the person fills ~89 % of the frame and hides the text — the script warns above 60 %. Mark such segments `"shot": "depth"` and they are generated as medium shots.

--- ## Cost reference (real runs) | Video | Generation | Credits | |---|---|---| | Livestream ad, 9:16, 27 s | 1 scene image + 5 Grok segments (720p) | **482** | | Tutorial Ep2, 16:9, 4:36 | 32 segments (full 720p / PiP 480p) + demos | ~3,250 | | Tutorial Ep3, 16:9, 5:54 | 30 new segments + 7 scene images, 17 segments reused | ~3,409 | Prices at the time of writing: Grok Video 1.5 — 720p 17 credits/s, 480p 10 credits/s; GPT Image 2.5 2k — 23 credits. Always confirm with the agent's live quote. ## Repository structure ``` skills/ digital-human-koubo/ main skill SKILL.md workflow the agent follows persona.json presenters, voice descriptions, prompt templates references/ style menu · packaging · playbook · install · research reports scripts/ build_tasks · rangedl · assemble · align · check_edit · cutout_video voicefx/unify · doctor · new_edit · make_assets templates/ huazi-916/ 9:16 data-driven talking-head template (edit.json) packaging/ 48-component kit + gallery project reference/ launch-169 · tutorial-169 · multihost-169 assets/ style previews · packaging gallery · avatar reference finance-explainer/ Style A engine (episode.json beat sheet, research helpers) docs/ README images, GIF previews, posters ``` ## Known pitfalls (all handled by the skill) - Grok occasionally **burns subtitles** into landscape clips even when told not to → frame check + re-shoot that segment. - whisper writes Chinese numbers as digits (九百九十九 → 999), so accuracy drops but the line is correct → listen before re-shooting. - Renoise's US CDN can truncate parallel downloads → `rangedl.py` downloads in 6 ranges with resume + decode check. - Grok 9:16 720p is **720×1280** — never stretch it to another ratio. - Expo easing never quite reaches the target (99.9 → rounds to 100) → counters snap to the exact value at the end. - Always mute the presenter video track; doubled audio a few ms apart sounds harsh (comb filtering). ## Responsible use - Use only your own face/voice or ones you have **explicit permission** to use. Never impersonate a real person or creator. - Every video carries an "AI digital human" label; scene and animal clips are marked "AI generated". - No made-up numbers, prices, offers or reviews — sample data on screen must be labelled as such. - Don't use web memes, film/TV stills or celebrity images — the meme components use original stickers generated from your own presenter. - Credits are spent only after you approve the quote. ## License & third-party - Code and docs: [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Berryxia (andyhuo520). - **[Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev/)** is used for rendering and has its own license: free for individuals and companies of up to 3 people; larger companies need a [company license](https://www.remotion.pro/). - Animated emoji: [Google Noto Emoji Animation](https://googlefonts.github.io/noto-emoji-animation/) (CC BY 4.0) — credit "Animated emoji: Google Noto" in your videos. - Maps: [world-atlas](https://github.com/topojson/world-atlas) (ISC; data from Natural Earth, public domain) · [d3-geo](https://github.com/d3/d3-geo), [topojson-client](https://github.com/topojson/topojson-client) (ISC). For maps involving China's borders in formally published content, check against applicable local standards. - Speech recognition: [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) (MIT). Generation runs on [Renoise](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) (your account, your credits); optional TTS by [Xiaomi MiMo](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/). - Course screenshots in the WorkBuddy demo come from the author's own course. items.readme:
# ex-USSR Kinship Research

![ex-USSR Kinship Research cover](docs/cover.jpg)

**An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes).** It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not.

The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but **the agent talks to you in your language**: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on. It quotes sources in their original spelling with a translation, and builds search queries in the languages of the records.

---

## What it does

- **Case intake and scope.** One research question, known facts, who may be alive, what is off-limits.
- **Reproducible registers.** Persons, artifacts, claims, relationships and a full search log (CSV), plus a final report template.
- **Historical jurisdiction model.** It resolves every event to the state, province, district, parish or civil registry *as of the event date*, not today's map.
- **Name-variant matrices.** Pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish forms, patronymics, maiden names and transliterations.
- **Source strategy.** Originals first, then official catalogs, indexes, published document collections, and only then trees and forums as leads.
- **Evidence protocol.** Claims get explainable statuses, not percentages: `hypothesis`, `single-source`, `corroborated`, `strongly-corroborated`, `contradicted`, `unresolved`. Copies and mirrors of one record share an `independence_group`, so they never count as independent proof.
- **Identity resolution.** Namesakes stay separate `person_id`s until distinguishing evidence appears: house number, parents, godparents, exact birth date or military unit.
- **Audit script.** It checks referential integrity and flags weak corroboration before you write conclusions. An independence group counts only when a cited artifact belongs to it, so corroboration cannot be declared into existence. It also checks the final report: every cited ID must exist in the registers and every status must match them. A summary shows what is still uncorroborated or marked illegible.
- **Final report.** Every relationship is laid out edge by edge, with contradictions, failed searches and concrete next steps.

Release history: [changelog](references/changelog.md).

## Install

Clone the repository into your agent's skills folder:

```bash
# Codex
git clone https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-research ~/.codex/skills/ex-ussr-kinship-research

# Claude Code (personal skills)
git clone https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-research ~/.claude/skills/ex-ussr-kinship-research
```

For a single project, put the folder in `.claude/skills/` inside the repository. The scripts need only Python 3 and the standard library; `build_pdf.py` also needs a Chromium-based browser.

## Use

Just describe the family question; the skill triggers on genealogy requests. For example:

- *"My great-grandfather was exiled to Kazakhstan in the 1930s. Help me find his parents in church records."*
- *"Here are scans of a marriage certificate and a soldier card. Check whether they are the same person and build the evidence chain."*
- *"Find the parish and the right FamilySearch film for a village in Podolia in the 1890s and read the births for the surname X."*

Keep private case data outside the skill's Git checkout. From the skill folder:

```bash
python scripts/init_case.py --case-dir ~/kinship-cases/my-case --research-question "Who were Maria's parents?" --subject-label "Maria"
python scripts/hash_artifact.py ~/kinship-cases/my-case/scans/marriage-1902.jpg   # SHA-256 for every saved artifact
python scripts/audit_evidence.py --case-dir ~/kinship-cases/my-case             # check registers before the final report
python scripts/build_pdf.py --html ~/kinship-cases/my-case/pdf-source/report.html --out ~/kinship-cases/my-case/report.pdf
```

`init_case.py` refuses to create a case inside the skill folder, including with
`--force`. Git ignores common legacy case-folder names as an additional safeguard;
check staged files before contributing, especially if moving an existing case.

`build_pdf.py` needs Chrome, Chromium or Edge installed (or `CHROME_PATH`). With `--png-dir` it also renders pages to PNG for review if `pypdfium2` is available.

Use static HTML with local or embedded images. Active HTML and network image sources are rejected; source links remain clickable. A failed render preserves any existing output PDF.

## Repository layout

```
SKILL.md                         main instructions (workflow, hard rules, language policy)
references/
  source-strategy.md             source hierarchy, query patterns, catalogs, archive requests
  evidence-protocol.md           artifact assessment, statuses, identity resolution, conflicts
  ex-ussr-locale-guide.md        jurisdictions, name variants, calendars, record types by period
  browser-and-captcha.md         browsing, sign-in, CAPTCHA hand-off, rate limits
  privacy-and-safety.md          living people, minors, DNA, sensitive findings
  seed-sources.md                curated starting resources with reliability classes
  field-lessons.md               practical lessons from a real case
  changelog.md                   release history
  photo-search.md                finding, identifying, dating and storing photos
  habsburg-galicia-bukovina.md   Galicia and Bukovina under the Habsburgs and after
assets/                          case intake, CSV registers, final report template,
                                 photos README template, readable PDF template (report-pdf.template.html)
scripts/                         init_case.py, hash_artifact.py, audit_evidence.py, build_pdf.py
evals/discovery-and-logic.yaml   trigger and reasoning test cases
tests/                           unit tests for audit_evidence.py (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests)
```

## Responsible use

- **Family history, not surveillance.** The skill refuses to look up current addresses, phones or accounts of living people, and it minimizes their data in reports.
- **No bypassing.** No CAPTCHA solving, no paywall, geo-block or rate-limit evasion, no leaked databases. Sign-ins are done by the user.
- **No uploads of your documents or DNA data** to third-party services without your explicit consent.
- **Sensitive findings** (deportation, repression, adoption, DNA surprises) are reported neutrally and only as far as the question requires.
- **Archive access rules change.** Always check the current official procedure before sending a request; the skill only drafts requests, it does not send them.

## Contributing

New sources are welcome. Add them to `references/seed-sources.md` with these fields: owner, jurisdiction, collection type, originals or index, stable IDs, access, restrictions, typical errors, date last checked. Please keep personal data out of examples.
